intro: Protects people who put money into private deposit schemes, chit-like schemes or 'financial establishments' that fail to repay. Commonly called the TNPID Act. Complaints go to the Economic Offences Wing (EOW) of TN Police. Overview of key points.

sections.p: Any person or company accepting deposits under any scheme in Tamil Nadu — except banks, government bodies and certain regulated entities. Covers schemes promising high returns, gold schemes and similar.

A financial establishment that fails to return deposits or pay promised interest or benefits, with fraudulent intent, commits an offence. Promoters, partners, directors, managers and employees responsible can be prosecuted.
The government can attach the money and property of the establishment — and of its promoters, directors and their relatives where bought with deposit money — to repay depositors.
A Special Court (TNPID Court) tries these cases, confirms attachments and orders sale of attached property to repay depositors proportionately.
